recipes.y: Serves 4 as mezze or 2–3 as a main
recipes.m: Gently fry the onion in vegetable oil for 12–15 minutes. Add garlic, then tomatoes, sugar, oregano, both paprikas, cinnamon, salt and pepper; cover and simmer 15 minutes. Add beans, hot water and more salt, cover and cook on low for 30 minutes. Stir in olive oil and parsley for 5 minutes, adjust seasoning and serve with feta.

recipes.n: Spicy kidney beans and baked eggs
recipes.m: Soften the onion in oil for about 5 minutes. Add paprika, cumin, herbs, soy sauce and vinegar for 2 minutes. Add beans, tomatoes, spinach and tomato puree, season, add half a tomato tin of hot water and simmer 5 minutes. Make four wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for about 5 minutes or to your liking.

recipes.n: Curried potato, greens and cheese frittata
recipes.m: Whisk and season the eggs, then mix in cheese and coriander. Slice the potatoes, brown them in butter and oil, and add to the eggs. Stir-fry the greens with curry powder, add mustard seeds, then combine everything. Pour into the wiped pan, set the edges over medium-high heat, then finish under a hot grill until cooked through.

recipes.p: 40 minutes, plus at least 1 hour chilling
recipes.m: Boil the potato and broad beans; skin the beans. Mash half the black beans with the potato, then roughly mash in the remaining beans. Soften onion and pepper in oil, add garlic and paprika, and mix into the beans. Toast and grind the cumin and coriander seeds, then add with lime and fresh coriander. Shape four burgers and chill at least 1 hour. Coat in cornmeal, fry both sides, then bake 10–15 minutes at 160°C. Serve in toasted buns with lettuce and avocado.

recipes.n: Green pea pulao with cardamom and almonds
recipes.m: Cook the rice and fluff it. Fry the cardamom in oil and butter for 30 seconds, add onion and cook gently for 10 minutes. Stir-fry the almonds for 3–4 minutes, then add peas and salt for 2 minutes. Fold in the rice. Fry the eggs separately and serve one on each bowl.

Mix and lightly crush the beans, cumin, oregano, chilli, spring onions, pepper and cheese. Divide between two tortillas and top with the remaining tortillas. Fry each quesadilla for 3–4 minutes per side. Toast the pumpkin seeds and serve over the quesadillas with avocado.

Heat the oven to 200°C/180°C fan. Toss cauliflower, paneer and onion with oil, yoghurt, garlic, spices and salt; roast for 30 minutes. Squeeze over lemon, scatter with coriander and serve with flatbreads.

Bring the stock and tomatoes to a gentle simmer. Soften onion in butter for 8–10 minutes, add garlic, then rice. Add the hot tomato stock a quarter at a time, stirring until absorbed, for 20–25 minutes. Season, stir in torn mozzarella, rest one minute and finish with olive oil.

Soft-boil the eggs for 6 minutes and cool in iced water. Fry curry paste, garlic and ginger in oil for 2 minutes. Add coconut milk, stock, soy sauce and sugar; simmer. Add tofu and simmer 5 minutes. Prepare noodles separately. Cook bok choy in the broth for 3–4 minutes, stir in lime juice, then serve over noodles with tofu, halved eggs, spring onions and coriander.

Wilt and drain the spinach. Boil the rice for 10 minutes and drain. Soften onion in butter, chop in the spinach and add the rice. Cool slightly, then mix in eggs, Parmesan and seasoning. Butter and crumb a tin, press in the mixture and bake for 25 minutes at 200°C.

recipes.n: Orzo with peas, herbs and Parmesan
recipes.m: Soften onion and minced parsley stalks in olive oil for about 10 minutes. Add peas, orzo and stock made with the water; simmer for the pasta cooking time, stirring occasionally. Add chopped parsley leaves in the last minute, then beat in Parmesan and serve.

recipes.n: Mediterranean-style pan-fried cheese with minty couscous salad
recipes.m: Mix couscous, cumin, onion and tomatoes; cover with boiling water and set aside. Mix garlic, mint, lemon zest and juice with half the oil. Dust halloumi in flour and fry in the remaining oil for 3–4 minutes per side. Fluff the couscous and stir through halloumi and mint dressing.
Roast chopped potatoes and bashed garlic with oil and seasoning for 30 minutes at 190°C. Add asparagus and halloumi and roast another 15 minutes. Discard the garlic and serve.

Cook the rice. Wilt the spinach. Grate and cook the carrots with sesame oil and sesame seeds. Grate and cook the courgette with ginger and spring onions. Cook the bean sprouts in soy sauce. Divide the rice among bowls, arrange the vegetables on top, add fried eggs and finish with toasted sesame seeds.

Soak noodles in boiling water for 6–8 minutes, drain and rinse. Mix the sauce ingredients. Stir-fry onion, then add garlic, pepper, carrot, spinach and noodles at 30-second intervals. Fry another minute, add sauce, boil vigorously and stir for 2–3 minutes until absorbed. Garnish with sesame seeds.

Heat oven to 220°C/200°C fan. Make a batter with flour, water and soy sauce, coat the cauliflower and add breadcrumbs. Bake 20–25 minutes. Mix the gochujang sauce ingredients, coat the cauliflower, then bake another 15–20 minutes. Finish with sesame seeds and spring onions.

Sauté broccoli in oil for one minute, add ginger for another minute, then set aside. Boil the water, add miso and simmer one minute. Remove from heat, soak noodles in the broth, then add tofu, spring onions, broccoli and coriander.

Cover noodles with boiling water until tender. Combine the shredded vegetables and herbs. Mix the dressing, season and pour over the vegetables. Drain and add the noodles, toss well, then serve with peanuts and red pepper.

Line a large pie tin with pastry. Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Mash cottage cheese into the potatoes, beat in sour cream and eggs, then stir through salt and onions. Fill the crust, top with Parmesan and bake 50 minutes until golden.

Boil and mash the potatoes, then mix with butter, egg yolk, Parmesan and seasoning. Soften onion in oil, add tomatoes and cook until soft. Butter and crumb a dish, press in half the potato, add the tomato mixture and cover with remaining potato. Top with crumbs and bake 30–40 minutes at 180°C/160°C fan.

Combine flour, salt and yeast, then gradually mix in the lukewarm water. Rest 5 minutes, knead 10 minutes, split in half and rise at least 30 minutes. Shape two 30cm bases, add toppings and bake about 10 minutes at 250°C.

Mix flour, salt, yeast, water and 20ml oil into a soft dough; rise one hour. Fold several times, rest 10 minutes, repeat, then chill 24 hours. Shape one ball and rest one hour. Stretch into a square, top with mozzarella and grated potato, season and drizzle with the remaining oil. Bake about 25 minutes at 220°C.

Rub butter into flour and salt, add yeast, then mix in Parmesan and milk to make a soft dough. Rise one hour, knead briefly and rise another hour. Roll 1cm thick, cut and roll into sticks. Bake 35–40 minutes at 160°C/140°C fan.

Cook the pasta. Warm oil and garlic, add sliced courgettes and plenty of pepper, then cook until browned. Add lemon juice and reduce slightly. Toss with drained pasta and a little extra oil, then garnish generously with Parmesan.

recipes.n: Pasta with red peppers and ricotta
recipes.m: Cook peppers, onion, olive oil, salt and chilli over medium-low heat until very soft, then blend smooth. Beat ricotta, Parmesan and milk into a soft cream. Cook pasta until al dente, toss with pepper sauce and top each serving with ricotta cream.
Heat oven to 180°C and line a muffin tray. Sift flour and salt, rub in butter, add remaining ingredients and mix softly. Spoon into cases, sprinkle with sugar and bake 20 minutes.

Heat oven to 180°C. Melt chocolate with butter, remove from heat and beat in eggs, sugar and flour. Pour into a greased, lined 25cm tin and bake 20 minutes until just set. Cool before cutting. Optional winter variation: sprinkle with cinnamon sugar before baking.

Cream butter and sugar, beat in egg and vanilla, then stir through flour and baking soda followed by chocolate chips. Drop tablespoons onto lined trays with space between. Bake 9–11 minutes at 180°C and cool on trays for 2 minutes.

Beat sugar, butter and peanut butter until fluffy. Add egg and vanilla, then flour, bicarbonate and salt. Shape walnut-sized balls, mark with a fork and chill at least 1 hour. Bake 10–12 minutes at 170°C.

recipes.p: A few hours or overnight chilling
recipes.m: Mix flour, raising agents and spices. Heat butter, sugar and syrup until smooth, then stir in the flour and enough beaten egg to form a dough. Chill for a few hours or overnight. Roll 2mm thick, cut shapes and bake about 12 minutes at 180°C.

Heat oven to 180°C and grease a 500g loaf tin. Soak oats in milk for 5–10 minutes. Mix flour, baking powder, sugar and ginger. Stir oil and syrup into the oats, add dry ingredients, pour into the tin and bake 25–30 minutes.
Mix butter and sugar. Stir in cocoa, vanilla sugar, water (or cold coffee) and oats. Shape into balls, roll in coconut and store chilled or frozen.

Heat oven to 180°C/160°C fan. Beat sponge ingredients until smooth, divide between two 20cm tins and bake 20–25 minutes. Cool. Whip cream with 50g sugar and vanilla. Spread one sponge with jam and the other with cream, then sandwich together.

Heat oven to 180°C/160°C fan. Cream butter, sugar and vanilla, beat in eggs, then fold in ground pistachios, flour, almonds, baking powder and soured cream. Bake 45–50 minutes in a 20cm tin. For ganache, pour steaming cream, syrup and salt over chocolate, stir smooth, thicken 10–15 minutes and spoon over the cake. Decorate with reserved pistachios.

Heat oven to 180°C. Mix flour, sugar, 3 tbsp cocoa and bicarbonate. Melt 250g butter with 250ml cola, then add with milk, eggs and vanilla. Bake about 40 minutes in a 24cm tin. Melt remaining butter, cola and cocoa, pour onto icing sugar, beat smooth and pour over the warm cake.

Heat oven to 160°C. Mix flour, baking powder, salt, spice and sugar, then beat in melted butter and eggs. Stir in apples, spoon into a 20cm tin and top with Demerara. Bake 1 hour, add almonds and bake another 15–25 minutes.

Heat oven to 190°C/170°C fan. Process dates until finely chopped. Melt butter and syrup with dates, remove from heat and mix in remaining ingredients. Press into a lined 20×30cm tin and bake 35–40 minutes. Cool before cutting.

recipes.n: Miso and brown butter Rice Krispies bars
recipes.m: Brown the butter, stir in marshmallows until melted, then whisk in miso and salt. Pour over Rice Krispies and mix thoroughly. Press into a lined 20cm tin, set at least 30 minutes and cut into bars.
Blend mango, yoghurt, milk, agave and cardamom until smooth. Stir in chia seeds, cover and chill for at least 8 hours or overnight. Serve topped with mango and mint.
